heading: Accounts, stores and staff
plain_line: Who can get into a store and act in it: the seller's account and login, staff and their permissions, and the business or organization behind one or more stores.
wont_do_removes: Seller accounts, staff and multiple stores would be outside Sharrwah's extent: the first build's design would leave it out, and no proposal would provide for it. Sharrwah could hardly run without accounts, so this mark is unlikely.
kept_anyway: Its statements stay as evidence for Q1, Q2, Q3, Q5, Q6, Q7 and Q8.
note: The platforms file accounts, staff and organizations under different names (Shopify's account and organization, Salla's profile and staff, WooCommerce's WordPress.com account, BigCommerce's staff accounts); no one platform's name covers them all. Shopify files its support for sellers here, with its account.

heading: Store settings and administration
plain_line: Running the store itself: its name, status and opening to buyers, domain, the messages it sends, and the platform's setup and status tools.
wont_do_removes: The store's own settings and messages would be outside Sharrwah's extent: the first build's design would leave it out, and no proposal would provide for it.
kept_anyway: Its statements stay as evidence for Q2, Q3, Q6 and Q8.
note: Each platform keeps these under its own settings menu, with different names and contents (General, Store settings, عام and المتجر, Store Profile, Status). Languages, which some of these menus hold, are in A-30.

heading: Plans, fees and support
plain_line: What a seller pays the platform and gets for it: subscription plans and their limits, fees on sales, billing, and the platform's support.
wont_do_removes: Plans, fees and support would be outside Sharrwah's extent: the first build's design would leave it out, and no proposal would provide for it. Sharrwah would then have no plan tiers or platform fees.
kept_anyway: Its statements stay as evidence for Q1, Q3, Q4, Q5, Q7 and Q8.
note: The platforms name this Plan, Billing, Store plan, الاشتراكات or Fees and Billing Terms; no one name covers them all. Salla's and Zid's support for sellers is here; Shopify files its support with its account (A-01), and WooCommerce's support policy is with its extensions (A-24).

heading: Products & inventory
plain_line: What a store sells and holds: products and their variants, categories, digital products, stock and the locations that hold it.
wont_do_removes: Products and stock would be outside Sharrwah's extent: the first build's design would leave it out, and no proposal would provide for it. Sharrwah could hardly sell without them, so this mark is unlikely.
kept_anyway: Its statements stay as evidence for Q3, Q5 and Q8.
note: Salla's options for taking donations on products are here; charity stores themselves are in A-34.

heading: Marketing and promotions
plain_line: The seller's own tools for selling more: discounts and coupons, campaigns, affiliates and ads, loyalty, and the blog and search-engine settings.
wont_do_removes: Marketing tools would be outside Sharrwah's extent: the first build's design would leave it out, and no proposal would provide for it.
kept_anyway: Its statements stay as evidence for Q2, Q5 and Q8.
note: Customer wallets, store credit and gift cards are in A-32, except BigCommerce's gift certificates, which BigCommerce files with its coupons and so are here.

heading: Customers
plain_line: The store's customers: their records and accounts, how they sign in, their consent and personal data, reviews and questions, and their tickets and complaints.
wont_do_removes: Customer records and service would be outside Sharrwah's extent: the first build's design would leave it out, and no proposal would provide for it. Sharrwah could hardly sell without customer records, so this mark is unlikely.
kept_anyway: Its statements stay as evidence for Q2, Q5 and Q8.
note: Zid Assurance (ضمان زد), which Zid offers to raise customers' trust, sits here with Zid's customers.

heading: Online store and themes
plain_line: How the storefront looks and is built: themes and where they are sold, pages and blogs, storefront search, and the engines theme builders use.
wont_do_removes: Themes and the storefront's design would be outside Sharrwah's extent: the first build's design would leave it out, and no proposal would provide for it.
kept_anyway: Its statements stay as evidence for Q8.
note: The platforms name this Online Store, Store design & themes, Store Design or Themes; no one name covers them all.

heading: Cart and checkout
plain_line: The buyer's cart and checkout: checkout settings and pages, abandoned carts, and the extensions and rules that change what checkout shows.
wont_do_removes: A checkout of Sharrwah's own would be outside Sharrwah's extent: the first build's design would leave it out, and no proposal would provide for it. Sharrwah could hardly sell without one, so this mark is unlikely.
kept_anyway: Its statements stay as evidence for Q5 and Q8.
note: The heading is ours because the platforms name this Checkout, Cart and checkout or Optimized checkout. Shopify, WooCommerce and BigCommerce give checkout an area of its own. Salla keeps it with payments (A-11) and Zid with its store settings (A-02).

heading: Orders
plain_line: Orders after they are placed: their statuses, payments recorded on them, edits, returns, refunds and cancellations.
wont_do_removes: Orders would be outside Sharrwah's extent: the first build's design would leave it out, and no proposal would provide for it. Sharrwah could hardly sell without them, so this mark is unlikely.
kept_anyway: Its statements stay as evidence for Q4, Q5, Q7 and Q8.

heading: Shipping and delivery
plain_line: Getting orders to buyers: shipping zones and rates, the platform's own shipping and its carriers, labels, fulfilment, and collecting cash on delivery.
wont_do_removes: Shipping and delivery would be outside Sharrwah's extent: the first build's design would leave it out, and no proposal would provide for it.
kept_anyway: Its statements stay as evidence for Q1, Q2, Q4, Q5, Q6 and Q8.

heading: How buyers pay: payment methods and providers
plain_line: How buyers pay: the payment methods a store offers, the providers and gateways behind them, pay-later and wallets, methods the seller records outside a provider such as bank transfer and cash on delivery, and who approves which provider.
wont_do_removes: Taking payment from buyers would be outside Sharrwah's extent: the first build's design would leave it out, and no proposal would provide for it. This would undo section B's items 4 and 5, so this mark is unlikely.
kept_anyway: Its statements stay as evidence for Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4, Q5, Q6, Q7 and Q8.
note: Each platform files its payment methods under its own name (Payments, الدفع, Payment Methods, Payment freedom); no one name covers them all. The platforms' own payment services, Salla Payments and BigCommerce Payments among them, are in A-12, and charity stores' payment gateways in A-34.

heading: The platform's own payment service, the seller's balance and payouts
plain_line: The platform's own payment service and the seller's money in it: Shopify Payments, Salla Payments and Salla's wallet, Zid Pay and Zid Wallet, WooPayments, and BigCommerce Payments; who may use it and where, verification, balances, payout timing, reserves, fees and disputes.
wont_do_removes: A payment service of Sharrwah's own, and any balance held for sellers, would be outside Sharrwah's extent: the first build's design would leave it out, and no proposal would provide for it. Your guard already stops any arrangement that holds sellers' money from going live without your decision.
kept_anyway: Its statements stay as evidence for Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4, Q5, Q6, Q7 and Q8. They are the main record of who holds sellers' money, which the pilot's deferred decisions turn on.
note: Each platform names its own service (Shopify Payments, Salla Payments or مدفوعات سلة, Zid Pay, WooPayments, BigCommerce Payments) or its wallet; no one name covers them all. Salla files the bank account its payouts go to with store verification (A-18), and its payment services contract with its terms (A-19).

heading: Financing and money products for sellers
plain_line: Money products the platform offers sellers beyond payments: business accounts and cards, loans, cash advances and other financing, and bill pay.
wont_do_removes: Lending and banking products for sellers would be outside Sharrwah's extent: the first build's design would leave it out, and no proposal would provide for it.
kept_anyway: Its statements stay as evidence for Q1, Q2, Q3, Q5, Q6 and Q8.
note: Shopify files these under Finance, Zid under تمويل زد, Salla as financial support, and WooCommerce under Stripe Capital; no one name covers them all.

heading: Taxes and duties
plain_line: Taxes on sales: tax rates and registrations, automated tax, invoices and e-invoicing such as the link with Saudi Arabia's ZATCA, duties and import taxes.
wont_do_removes: Tax handling would be outside Sharrwah's extent: the first build's design would leave it out, and no proposal would provide for it.
kept_anyway: Its statements stay as evidence for Q1, Q2, Q3, Q6 and Q8.

heading: Per-country versions of one store
plain_line: Separate versions of one store for different countries, each with its own settings, which Shopify, Salla and Zid call markets; with Shopify's Managed Markets, international domains and geolocation.
wont_do_removes: Per-country versions of one store would be outside Sharrwah's extent: the first build's design would leave it out, and no proposal would provide for it. A store could still sell to buyers in other countries, as one version: the countries a store sells to are in A-16, and languages and currencies in A-30 and A-31, so this mark removes none of them.
kept_anyway: Its statements stay as evidence for Q1, Q2, Q3, Q5, Q6, Q7 and Q8.
note: The heading is ours: Shopify, Salla and Zid name this Markets, Multi-market or الأسواق, and WooCommerce and BigCommerce have no such setting. Languages and currencies, which the platforms keep apart from markets, are in A-30 and A-31.

heading: Where the platform operates, and where a store sells
plain_line: Where the platform operates and where a store sells: the countries the platform serves or doesn't, the country a seller gives at sign-up, the payment providers it suggests for each country, and the countries a store sells and ships to and keeps for addresses.
wont_do_removes: Choosing where Sharrwah operates, and the countries a store sells and ships to, would be outside Sharrwah's extent: the first build's design would leave it out, and no proposal would provide for it. Sharrwah must operate somewhere, so this mark is unlikely.
kept_anyway: Its statements stay as evidence for Q1, Q2, Q3, Q5, Q6, Q7 and Q8.
note: Shopify, Salla and Zid each list the places they serve under a different name (Unsupported countries and regions, مدعوم في, ZID is available in). WooCommerce's selling and shipping locations, Zid's store countries and cities, and BigCommerce's Geography are the store's own settings, and are here too, with Zid Egypt, Zid's company in Egypt.

heading: What may not be sold, and who may not use the platform
plain_line: What may not be sold and who may not use the platform: restricted and prohibited businesses, acceptable use, sanctions and export rules.
wont_do_removes: Rules on what may not be sold would be outside Sharrwah's extent: the first build's design would leave it out, and no proposal would provide for it.
kept_anyway: Its statements stay as evidence for Q2, Q3, Q5, Q6 and Q8.
note: WooCommerce and BigCommerce give these rules an area of their own. The others keep them elsewhere: Shopify's sanctions with where it operates (A-16), its Acceptable Use Policy with its terms (A-19) and Shopify Payments' prohibited businesses with its payment service (A-12); Zid's prohibited activities with Zid Pay (A-12); and Salla's with its terms and verification (A-19 and A-18).

heading: Store Verification
plain_line: Opening a store and verifying the business behind it: the documents and checks each country requires, and the bank account that receives the store's money.
wont_do_removes: Verifying sellers would be outside Sharrwah's extent: the first build's design would leave it out, and no proposal would provide for it.
kept_anyway: Its statements stay as evidence for Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4, Q5, Q6 and Q8.

heading: Terms, and the company a seller contracts with
plain_line: The terms a seller agrees to and the company it contracts with, which on several platforms depends on the seller's country; governing law, suspension and termination.
wont_do_removes: Published terms and contracting companies would be outside Sharrwah's extent: the first build's design would leave it out, and no proposal would provide for it. Sharrwah could hardly operate without terms, so this mark is unlikely.
kept_anyway: Its statements stay as evidence for Q1, Q2, Q3, Q5, Q6 and Q8.
note: Each platform publishes its own set of agreements; no one name covers them all.

heading: Privacy and security
plain_line: Personal data and security: who controls and who processes data, where it is stored and sent, the outside companies that process data for the platform (which the platforms call subprocessors), card security, and what the store sends back to the platform.
wont_do_removes: Privacy and security would be outside Sharrwah's extent: the first build's design would leave it out, and no proposal would provide for it. Sharrwah could hardly operate without them, so this mark is unlikely.
kept_anyway: Its statements stay as evidence for Q1, Q2, Q3, Q6 and Q8.

heading: Sales channels
plain_line: Selling beyond the store's own site: sales channels, marketplaces (including the platform's own, such as Zid's Mazeed), social channels, and several storefronts from one store.
wont_do_removes: Sales channels and marketplaces would be outside Sharrwah's extent: the first build's design would leave it out, and no proposal would provide for it.
kept_anyway: Its statements stay as evidence for Q1, Q3, Q5, Q6 and Q8.
note: Shopify's agentic storefronts, through which AI agents shop for buyers, are here with its sales channels.

heading: Point of sale (POS)
plain_line: Selling in person: point-of-sale apps, card readers, cash and the hardware behind them.
wont_do_removes: Selling in person would be outside Sharrwah's extent: the first build's design would leave it out, and no proposal would provide for it.
kept_anyway: Its statements stay as evidence for Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4, Q5, Q6, Q7 and Q8.

heading: B2B
plain_line: Selling to businesses: company accounts, quotes, and payment terms such as invoices paid later.
wont_do_removes: Selling to businesses would be outside Sharrwah's extent: the first build's design would leave it out, and no proposal would provide for it.
kept_anyway: Its statements stay as evidence for Q4, Q5 and Q8.
note: Only Shopify and BigCommerce give selling to businesses an area. Salla's plans list selling to businesses and wholesale, which the concern map left out of its scope, and WooCommerce offers it through extensions (A-24) and B2B payments (A-11). Shopify's catalogs, which serve business customers and markets alike, are in A-33.

heading: Apps
plain_line: Apps and extensions a seller adds from the platform's own store of apps, and the services listed there.
wont_do_removes: A store of apps for sellers would be outside Sharrwah's extent: the first build's design would leave it out, and no proposal would provide for it. Payment methods that come through apps, which section B's item 5 names, would go with it.
kept_anyway: Its statements stay as evidence for Q5 and Q8.

heading: Build & integrate
plain_line: Building on the platform: its APIs, webhooks, the permissions apps ask for (which Shopify calls access scopes) and how apps are authorized, and storefronts built apart from its themes.
wont_do_removes: Building on Sharrwah by outside developers would be outside Sharrwah's extent: the first build's design would leave it out, and no proposal would provide for it.
kept_anyway: Its statements stay as evidence for Q8.
note: WooCommerce MCP, through which AI tools act on a store, is here with WooCommerce's developer tools.

heading: Partners and services for sellers
plain_line: The platform's partners and the services sellers get through it: partner programs and their payouts, agencies, migration and growth services.
wont_do_removes: Partner programs and services would be outside Sharrwah's extent: the first build's design would leave it out, and no proposal would provide for it.
kept_anyway: Its statements stay as evidence for Q8.
note: The platforms name this Partner Program, Partners, Merchant Services or زد نمو; no one name covers them all. Salla's names here are its Partners portal's menus, for partners rather than for sellers.

heading: Analytics
plain_line: Reports and analytics on a store's sales, payments, customers and products.
wont_do_removes: Reports and analytics would be outside Sharrwah's extent: the first build's design would leave it out, and no proposal would provide for it.
kept_anyway: Its statements stay as evidence for Q4 and Q8.

heading: AI and automation
plain_line: AI tools and automation for sellers, and AI agents that shop on a buyer's behalf.
wont_do_removes: AI tools and automation would be outside Sharrwah's extent: the first build's design would leave it out, and no proposal would provide for it.
kept_anyway: Its statements stay as evidence for Q8.
note: Only Shopify and BigCommerce give these an area; each names it differently (Shopify Flow and AI-powered tools, BigAI). Other AI features sit where the platforms file them: Salla's AI Connector and writing tools in A-02, WooCommerce MCP in A-25, WooCommerce's AI guidelines in A-19, and Shopify's agentic storefronts in A-21.

heading: Mobile app
plain_line: A store's own mobile app for its customers.
wont_do_removes: A store app would be outside Sharrwah's extent: the first build's design would leave it out, and no proposal would provide for it.
kept_anyway: Its statements stay as evidence for Q8.

heading: Languages
plain_line: The languages a store is shown in, and translating its content.
wont_do_removes: A store in more than one language would be outside Sharrwah's extent: the first build's design would leave it out, and no proposal would provide for it.
kept_anyway: Its statements stay as evidence for Q1 and Q8.
note: Shopify, Salla and BigCommerce name languages apart from currencies. Zid sets a store's languages and currencies on one settings page (لغة وعملات المتجر), which is in A-31. WooCommerce offers languages through extensions, in its International and localization category (A-24).

heading: Currencies
plain_line: The store's currency, the currencies prices are shown and paid in, and currency conversion.
wont_do_removes: Prices and payments in more than one currency would be outside Sharrwah's extent: the first build's design would leave it out, and no proposal would provide for it. A store would have one currency.
kept_anyway: Its statements stay as evidence for Q1, Q2, Q3, Q5, Q7 and Q8.
note: Zid sets a store's languages and currencies on one settings page (لغة وعملات المتجر), so Zid's languages are here too.

heading: Gift cards, store credit and customer wallets
plain_line: Value a buyer holds and spends in the store: gift cards, store credit, and customer wallets with cashback.
wont_do_removes: Gift cards, store credit and customer wallets would be outside Sharrwah's extent: the first build's design would leave it out, and no proposal would provide for it.
kept_anyway: Its statements stay as evidence for Q2, Q5 and Q8.
note: The heading is ours: Shopify files gift cards with products and store credit with customers, and Salla and Zid file customer wallets with marketing. No one name covers them all. BigCommerce files its gift certificates with its coupons, in A-05.

heading: Catalogs and price lists
plain_line: Sets of products and prices offered to particular buyers: catalogs for one of Shopify's markets or for a business customer, and price lists for a sales channel or a customer group.
wont_do_removes: Catalogs and price lists would be outside Sharrwah's extent: the first build's design would leave it out, and no proposal would provide for it.
kept_anyway: Its statements stay as evidence for Q1, Q7 and Q8.
note: The heading is ours, joining Shopify's Catalogs and BigCommerce's Price Lists; no one name covers both.

heading: Charity stores
plain_line: Stores run by charities, and the payment gateways open to them.
wont_do_removes: Charity stores would be outside Sharrwah's extent: the first build's design would leave it out, and no proposal would provide for it.
kept_anyway: Its statements stay as evidence for Q2, Q3, Q5, Q6 and Q8.
note: The heading is Salla's help-centre category, 🤝 Charity stores, without its emoji, so it is marked as ours. No other platform gives charity stores an area. Salla's donation options on products are in A-04, Zid's charity business type in A-18, and Shopify's non-profit business entity in A-01.
